- design: Create a design canvas — a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces — posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including Markdown ones — format is part of the design pass, never a speed shortcut.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, handing the viewer a file to save, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.

Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").

/-
Imscribing/NumberTheory/ErdosStrausProof.lean

Erdős–Straus: what is proved, and what is open.

The conjecture is that `4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z` has a positive integer solution
for every `n ≥ 2`. It is OPEN. What is settled is every congruence class except
one: the residues `n ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with `3 ∤ n` are the standing gap, and every
other `n` is handled by an explicit parametric family.

This file previously claimed the whole conjecture, in 1175 lines, and three
things were wrong with it.

**The statement was empty.** `structure Solution` carried the equation
`4*x*y*z = n*(y*z + x*z + x*y)` with `n` appearing nowhere in its parameters,
and the main theorem read `theorem erdos_straus (n : ℕ) (hn : n ≥ 2) :
∃ (sol : Solution)`. The conclusion does not mention `n`. Whatever `n` the
structure's equation referred to, it was not the `n` the theorem quantified
over, so the theorem said only that some solution of some instance exists.
`Solution` now takes `n` as a parameter and the theorem concludes about that
`n`.

**One family was arithmetically false.** `solve_mod12_9` set `x = 3k+3` and
`y = z = (12k+9)(k+1)`. At `k = 0` that is `1/3 + 1/9 + 1/9 = 5/9`, against
`4/9`. The two tails are each half of what they should be: `4/n − 1/(3k+3)`
is `1/(n(k+1))`, and splitting it in two gives `y = z = 2n(k+1)`. Corrected
below and proved.

**It constructed a solution for the open case.** `solve_mod4_1_not3` claimed to
build a solution for `n ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with `3 ∤ n` out of a CRT search for a
`d` with `d ≡ 3 (mod 4)`, `d ≡ 0 (mod 3)`, `d ≡ −n (mod 5)`. That case is the
conjecture. It is stated here as a Prop and not constructed.

The file also never compiled — it imported `Mathlib.NumberTheory.Primes`, which
does not exist in this toolchain — and it was absent from the lakefile, so
nothing ever checked any of the above.

Author: Lando⊗⊙perator
-/
import Mathlib.Tactic

namespace ErdosStraus

/-- A solution to `4/n = 1/x + 1/y + 1/z`, cleared of denominators. `n` is a
parameter: without it the equation refers to a variable the statement does not
quantify over. -/
structure Solution (n : ℕ) where
  x : ℕ
  y : ℕ
  z : ℕ
  hx : 0 < x
  hy : 0 < y
  hz : 0 < z
  hmain : 4 * x * y * z = n * (y * z + x * z + x * y)

-- ============================================================
-- §1  The parametric families
-- ============================================================

/-- `n` even, `n = 2m`: `4/(2m) = 1/m + 1/(m+1) + 1/(m(m+1))`. -/

import Mathlib
import Imscribing.Classical.Szemeredi

/-!
# Erdős's conjecture on arithmetic progressions, at every `k`

If `Σ 1/a` over `A` diverges, `A` contains a `k`-term arithmetic progression —
reduced, for every `k`, to a counting bound past exponent one.

The `k = 3` development proves this through Mathlib's `ThreeAPFree` and
`rothNumberNat`, and leans on `addRothNumber_Ico` for translation invariance.
Neither of those exists for `k ≥ 4`. What is 3-specific is exactly that one
lemma, so it is proved here directly: `card_le_r_k` shifts a progression-free
subset of any interval down to `range N` and observes that a progression in the
image lifts back by adding the offset.

Everything after it is indifferent to `k`. The dyadic decomposition, the block
estimate, the transport from a subtype to an indicator and the comparison with a
`p`-series never mention the length of a progression; they mention only the
counting function that bounds it.

The conclusion is therefore uniform in `k`: given

    r_k(N) ≤ C·N/(log N)^(1+ε)    for some ε > 0 and all large N,

divergent reciprocals force a `k`-term progression. At `k = 3` such a bound is
known (Bloom–Sisask; Kelley–Meka is stronger). For `k ≥ 4` none is known, and
this file states precisely which inequality would close the case.
-/

open Finset
open scoped Classical BigOperators

namespace Millennium.ErdosProblems.APFree

open Imscribing.Classical.Szemeredi

/-- `A` carries no `k`-term progression with positive common difference. The set
form of `Szemeredi.APFree`. -/
def SetAPFree (k : ℕ) (A : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a d : ℕ, 0 < d → ¬ (∀ i, i < k → a + i * d ∈ A)

/-- Progression-freeness passes to any finite subset. -/
theorem apFree_of_subset {k : ℕ} {A : Set ℕ} (hA : SetAPFree k A)
    (S : Finset ℕ) (hS : ∀ x ∈ S, x ∈ A) : APFree k S := by

Here's the state, all on `tooling/prooflift` (every `crystalline/erdos-*` branch is already an ancestor of HEAD — nothing stranded).

## Erdős–Straus

`Imscribing/NumberTheory/ErdosStrausProof.lean` (174 lines, 6 theorems, **0 sorry, 0 axiom**, olean built) is the live one. It replaced a 1175-line file that claimed the whole conjecture and was wrong three ways: the `Solution` structure didn't mention `n` so the main theorem was vacuous; `solve_mod12_9` was arithmetically false at `k=0` (`1/3+1/9+1/9 = 5/9 ≠ 4/9`, tails each half-sized — corrected to `y=z=2n(k+1)`); and `solve_mod4_1_not3` "constructed" the open case out of a CRT search. It also never compiled and was absent from the lakefile, so nothing had ever checked it.

What stands proved: explicit parametric families for `n` even, `n ≡ 0, 2, 3 (mod 4)`, and `n ≡ 1 (mod 4)` with `3 | n`. The surviving class is `n ≡ 1 (mod 4), 3 ∤ n`, stated as a Prop and not constructed — the price-zero half matches what the branch name says.

`Imscribing/Classical/ErdosStrausDecomposition.lean` (210 lines, 10 theorems) carries the same congruence-class work with the mod-4-one case isolated as a named open Prop.

**Two stale copies** are on disk and in neither the lakefile nor any build: `Imscribing/ErdosStrausDecomposition.lean` (a StructoForge-generated `Imscription` record asserting the full conjecture as settled) and `Imscribing/Conjectures/ErdosStrausDecomposition.lean` (30 lines, now pure post-mortem prose about the five bad `sorry`s it used to hold). Three copies of one name; the one being read is the `Classical` one.

## Erdős 3 (AP in divergent-reciprocal sets)

`Imscribing/Millennium/Erdos/APFreeReduction.lean` closes `k = 3` from a Roth bound and nothing else, and reduces every `k ≥ 4` to a single named inequality: `r_k(N) ≤ C·N/(log N)^(1+ε)`. What was 3-specific was exactly `addRothNumber_Ico`; that's now proved directly as `card_le_r_k` by shifting into `range N`, so the dyadic decomposition, block estimate and `p`-series comparison are all uniform in `k`. `Imscribing/Classical/Szemeredi.lean` defines `r_k` and proves Behrend, so those bounds are statements about a real object.

## Erdős–Fuchs, Turán, Problem 16

- `ProofModules/ErdosFuchs.lean` — the two `sorry`ed statements were **false**, not unproved: they asserted the average `(1/N)∑r_A(n)` diverges for a basis of square-root density. Proved instead that it's bounded by `C²` whenever `|A ∩ [0,N)| ≤ C√N`. 0 sorry.
- `ErdosTuranBound` (549 lines, 13 thm), `ErdosTuranReduction`, `ErdosTuranSmallC`, `Erdos/ErdosTuranAP`, `ErdosKacInterval`, `ErdosProblem16` (the false step is a proved refutation), `ErdosProblems.lean` (643 lines, 14 thm) — all 0 sorry, 0 axiom.
- The three `ErdosFormalize` batches compile; they had been written against a Mathlib that does not exist.

## Axiom cost

Only two Erdős files pay any: `ErdosPropertyP.lean` (3 axioms — existence of a √-density Property-P set, the `N^(1-c)` upper bound, and summability of reciprocals) and `ErdosLaxDivergence.lean` (1 axiom, `erdos_lax_axiom`, the unimodular-product divergence).

## The stub corpus

`Millennium/Erdos/Problems/` holds 33 files, 30 with a live `sorry` — these are statements, not attempts. Two are in the lakefile (`Problem0003`, `Problem0041`). `Problem1135.lean` is the outlier: 639 lines of Collatz scaffolding with 13 sorries, several labelled as the genuinely hard part. The 24 named modules beside `Problems/` (SidonCounting, UnitDistance, PomeranceSDR, SchutteTournament, …) are the built machinery and are all in the lakefile.

The only dirty working-tree files are the two `Scratch/ProverScratch*.lean`, unrelated to Erdős.

########## da81ae3
Pulled the three papers, and one of my claims was wrong

Checked the literature instead of citing it from memory, and found I had
conflated two different shapes.

Bloom–Sisask (arXiv:2007.03528), abstract verbatim: |A| ≪ N/(log N)^{1+c} for
absolute c > 0. Exactly the shape erdos_conjecture_of_bound consumes, past
exponent one. k = 3 closes.

Green–Tao III (arXiv:1705.01703): r_4(N) ≪ N(log N)^{-c}, absolute c > 0, "the
limit of our methods". Their own notational convention records 0 < c ≪ 1. Right
shape, exponent below one.

Leng–Sah–Sawhney (arXiv:2402.17995), Theorem 1.1 verbatim: "Fix k ≥ 5. There is
c_k ∈ (0,1) such that r_k(N) ≪ N exp(-(log log N)^{c_k})." The interval is
theirs.

The error: I had written that a log-log bound is insufficient at any exponent and
attached Leng–Sah–Sawhney to that claim. The theorem I proved is about
1/(log j)^c, which is what Gowers' N/(log log N)^c gives. Leng–Sah–Sawhney give
exp(-(log j)^{c_k}) at the dyadic scale, which is a different shape, and it is
NOT insufficient at any exponent — it converges precisely when c_k > 1.

So two more theorems, and they change what the open cases are.
not_summable_exp_neg_log_rpow: the shape diverges for c ≤ 1.
summable_exp_neg_log_rpow: it converges for c > 1.

Which makes both open cases the same kind of thing. At k = 4 a polylogarithmic
exponent must cross one; at k ≥ 5 a log-log exponent must. Each is a single
number in a published theorem, and in each the authors state their number is
below the threshold. Not a programme — a constant.

Note for the next fight with the elaborator: the convergence proof timed out at a
million heartbeats, and none of the analysis was to blame. `Summable.of_nonneg_of_le`
applied against `(summable_nat_add_iff M).mpr ?_` leaves a metavariable to be
solved by higher-order unification, which does not terminate usefully. Naming the
comparison series first and passing it explicitly compiles the whole thing in
twenty seconds.

which is harmonic. That is the knife-edge, and it is where Roth's own bound sits
at k = 3.

exponent one. At k = 3 that is Bloom–Sisask. At k = 4 a bound of the right SHAPE

the door there is not "prove something polylogarithmic" but "push a known
exponent past 1". For k ≥ 5 the shape itself is not yet reached.

what is true. The module docstring now states the mathematical situation (why

-- ─── Opaque definitions ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────

/-- `A` carries no `k`-term arithmetic progression with positive common
difference. -/
def APFree (k : ℕ) (A : Finset ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ a d : ℕ, 0 < d → ¬ (∀ i, i < k → a + i * d ∈ A)

/-- `r_k k N`: the largest size of a `k`-AP-free subset of `range N`.

Defined, not declared. It was `opaque r_k (k N : ℕ) : ℕ` — a constant with no
body — and every bound below was then a bound on an arbitrary function of two
naturals, satisfiable by `fun _ _ => 0` and therefore incapable of discharging
anything. A definition costs nothing here: the largest cardinality among
progression-free subsets is a supremum over a finite family. -/
noncomputable def r_k (k N : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  ((Finset.range N).powerset.filter (fun A => APFree k A)).sup
    (fun A : Finset ℕ => A.card)

/-- The definition has content: a progression-free subset of `range N` has at
most `N` elements. An opaque symbol admits no such fact. -/
theorem r_k_le (k N : ℕ) : r_k k N ≤ N := by
  unfold r_k
  refine Finset.sup_le ?_
  intro A hA
  rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_powerset] at hA
  calc A.card ≤ (Finset.range N).card := Finset.card_le_card hA.1
    _ = N := Finset.card_range N

/-- The k-term arithmetic progression counting operator Λ_k(f). -/
=== bs/km axioms
/-- **Bloom–Sisask upper bound at k = 3** (arXiv:2007.03528).

`r₃(N) ≤ C·N/(log N)^(1+c)` for some `c > 0` — the first bound past exponent one,
which is the threshold this corollary needs: at `c = 0` the dyadic comparison
series is harmonic and gives nothing.

Weaker than `kelley_meka_upper_bound` and stated separately because it is the
shape the consumer wants. `Problem0003.erdos_problem_3_k3_of_roth_bound` takes a
hypothesis of exactly this form and returns Erdős 3 at k = 3. -/
axiom bloom_sisask_upper_bound :
  ∃ (C c : ℝ) (N₀ : ℕ), 0 ≤ C ∧ 0 < c ∧ 1 ≤ N₀ ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, N₀ ≤ N →
    (rothNumberNat N : ℝ) ≤ C * N / (Real.log N) ^ (1 + c)

/-- **Kelley–Meka upper bound at k = 3** (arXiv:2302.05537).

Stated about `rothNumberNat`, which Mathlib defines, rather than about a symbol
of this file. A bound on an opaque constant is inert: it cannot be contradicted
and it cannot be used. This one has content — `Problem0003.summable_blocks_of_log_bound`
consumes a bound of exactly this shape and returns the summability that closes
Erdős 3 at k = 3.

Still an axiom, because the theorem is not formalized anywhere. That is the
honest remaining debt, and it is one line rather than eight. -/
axiom kelley_meka_upper_bound :
  ∃ (c : ℝ) (N₀ : ℕ), c > 0 ∧ ∀ N : ℕ, N ≥ N₀ →
    (rothNumberNat N : ℝ) ≤ (N : ℝ) * Real.exp (-c * (Real.log (N : ℝ)) ^ (1/11 : ℝ))

/-- Szemerédi's Theorem (1975): For k ≥ 3, r_k(N) = o(N). -/

`summable_exp_neg_log_rpow` they converge for `c_k > 1`. So the case closes when

published theorem, and in both the number is stated by its authors to be below

-/

Divergent reciprocals force a `k`-term arithmetic progression, given

\begin{document}
\title{\textbf{Progressions from Divergent Reciprocals, at Every $k$}}
\author{C.\ Lando Mills\\
Trabuco Canyon, California\\
\texttt{c.landonmills@gmail.com}\\
ORCID: \href{https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0003-0552}{0000-0003-0003-0552}}
\date{17 August 2026}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
Szemer\'edi's theorem takes positive upper density as its hypothesis; the
Erd\H{o}s--Tur\'an conjecture takes the divergence of $\sum 1/a_n$. The second
hypothesis is strictly weaker, and the primes separate them.

Under the weaker hypothesis the conjecture reduces, at every $k$, to a single
inequality about the counting function: if $r_k(N) \le CN/(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$
for some $\varepsilon > 0$, then a set of divergent reciprocals contains a
$k$-term progression. The reduction never mentions the length of a progression.
What is $3$-specific in the usual account is exactly one lemma --- translation
invariance of the counting function --- and it is proved here directly, for all
$k$.

The threshold is sharp in both directions, and we prove it so. A bound at
exponent one gives a harmonic comparison series and closes nothing; a bound of
the shape $N/(\log\log N)^{c}$ fails for every $c$; a bound of the shape
$N\exp(-(\log\log N)^{c})$ fails for $c \le 1$ and succeeds for $c > 1$. Against
the published bounds this places each open case at a single constant.
Behrend's construction shows the decay at $k = 3$ admits no power saving.
\end{abstract}

\section{The two hypotheses}

Let $A = \{a_1 < a_2 < \cdots\} \subseteq \mathbb{N}$.

\begin{itemize}
\item[] \textbf{(D)} \quad
$\displaystyle \limsup_{N} \frac{|A \cap [0,N)|}{N} > 0$.
\item[] \textbf{(R)} \quad
$\displaystyle \sum_n \frac{1}{a_n} = \infty$.
\end{itemize}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:implies}
Hypothesis (D) implies hypothesis (R).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
The finite form suffices: if $A \cap [0,N)$ has at least $\varepsilon N$
elements, then those elements contribute at least
\[
  \varepsilon N \cdot \frac1N \;=\; \varepsilon
\]
to $\sum_{a \in A,\ a < N} 1/a$, since each is at most $N$. Applying this along a
sequence of scales $N_1 < N_2 < \cdots$ on which the density stays above
$\varepsilon$, and which grows fast enough that the ranges are disjoint, gives
divergence.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:strict}
The implication is strict: the primes satisfy (R) and fail (D).
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\sum_p 1/p$ diverges, while $\pi(N)/N \to 0$.
\end{proof}

\[
  \boxed{\;\text{(D)} \Longrightarrow \text{(R)}, \qquad
  \text{(R)} \nRightarrow \text{(D)}. \;}
\]

Szemer\'edi's theorem and the Erd\H{o}s--Tur\'an conjecture are therefore
different statements, and the latter is the stronger. \Cref{prop:strict} is not
a curiosity about a hard example: it says that any argument routed through
positive lower density is, under (R), not merely unproved but unavailable. No
$\varepsilon$ satisfies $\varepsilon N \le |A \cap [0,N)|$ for all $N$ when $A$
is the primes.

\section{The counting function}

\begin{definition}
\label{def:rk}
$A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ is \emph{$k$-progression-free} if there are no
$a$ and $d > 0$ with $a + id \in A$ for all $i < k$. Write $r_k(N)$ for the
largest cardinality of a $k$-progression-free subset of $[0,N)$.
\end{definition}

The supremum is over a finite family, so $r_k$ is a definition and not a
declaration; $r_k(N) \le N$ is then a fact about it rather than an assumption
placed upon it. This matters for what follows: a bound imposed on a symbol with
no body is satisfied by the zero function and discharges nothing.

\begin{lemma}[Translation invariance, at every $k$]
\label{lem:shift}
If $A \subseteq [m, m+N)$ is $k$-progression-free, then $|A| \le r_k(N)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $B = \{x - m : x \in A\} \subseteq [0,N)$. Subtraction by $m$ is injective on
$A$, so $|B| = |A|$. If $B$ carried a progression $a + id$, $i < k$, $d > 0$,
then $(a+m) + id$ lies in $A$ for each $i < k$, a progression in $A$ with the
same common difference. So $B$ is $k$-progression-free and $|B| \le r_k(N)$.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:shift} is the only step in this paper that is usually taken from
three-term machinery. For $k = 3$ it is available as a statement about
$\mathrm{rothNumberNat}$; for $k \ge 4$ there is no such statement to take, and
the proof above is the reason none is needed. Everything after it is indifferent
to $k$.

\begin{corollary}
\label{cor:block}
A $k$-progression-free $A$ meets the dyadic block $[2^j, 2^{j+1})$ in at most
$r_k(2^j)$ points.
\end{corollary}

\section{The reduction}

\begin{lemma}[Dyadic decomposition]
\label{lem:dyadic}
For any $g : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}$ and any $J$,
\[
  \sum_{i=1}^{2^J - 1} g(i)
    \;=\; \sum_{j<J} \ \sum_{i = 2^j}^{2^{j+1}-1} g(i).
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{lemma}[Block estimate]
\label{lem:block}
If $A$ is $k$-progression-free then
\[
  \sum_{i = 2^j}^{2^{j+1}-1} \mathbf{1}_A(i)\,\frac1i \;\le\; \frac{r_k(2^j)}{2^j}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The sum has at most $r_k(2^j)$ nonzero terms by \Cref{cor:block}, and each is at
most $1/2^j$ because the block begins there.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:blocks}
If $\sum_j r_k(2^j)/2^j$ converges, then every $k$-progression-free set has
convergent reciprocal sum.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Pass from the subtype to the indicator $\mathbf{1}_A(m)/m$ on $\mathbb{N}$, and
bound partial sums: push $N$ out to $2^N$, drop the index $0$, split by
\Cref{lem:dyadic} and bound each block by \Cref{lem:block}. The partial sums are
monotone and bounded by the tsum, so the series converges.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[The exponent is the content]
\label{prop:logbound}
If $r_k(N) \le CN/(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon > 0$, some
$C \ge 0$ and all $N \ge N_0$, then $\sum_j r_k(2^j)/2^j$ converges.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Substituting $N = 2^j$ turns the bound into $Kj^{-(1+\varepsilon)}$ with
$K = C/(\log 2)^{1+\varepsilon}$, and a $p$-series with $p > 1$ converges.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[Erd\H{o}s's conjecture at $k$, from a counting bound]
\label{thm:main}
Fix $k$. Suppose there are $\varepsilon > 0$, $C \ge 0$ and $N_0 \ge 1$ with
\[
  r_k(N) \;\le\; \frac{CN}{(\log N)^{1+\varepsilon}} \qquad (N \ge N_0).
\]
Then every $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$ with $\sum_{a \in A} 1/a = \infty$ contains a
$k$-term arithmetic progression with positive common difference.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Contrapositive. If $A$ carries no such progression it is $k$-progression-free,
so \Cref{prop:logbound} and \Cref{prop:blocks} make $\sum_{a \in A} 1/a$
convergent.
\end{proof}

At $k = 3$ the hypothesis of \Cref{thm:main} is a theorem, and the conjecture
closes. For $k \ge 4$ it is open, and by the theorem it is the whole of what is
open.

\section{The threshold, in both directions}

\Cref{thm:main} consumes a bound past exponent one. The following say that
``past exponent one'' is not a convenience of the proof.

\begin{proposition}[The knife-edge]
\label{prop:edge}
For every $C > 0$, the series $\sum_j C/(j \log 2)$ diverges.
\end{proposition}

A bound $r_k(N) \le CN/\log N$ gives dyadic terms $C/(j\log 2)$, which is
harmonic. That is where Roth's own bound sits at $k = 3$, and it is why every
Roth bound before Bloom and Sisask left the problem open.

\begin{proposition}[The log-log shape is insufficient at every exponent]
\label{prop:loglog}
For every $c > 0$, the series $\sum_j 1/(\log j)^{c}$ diverges.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
$\log j \le c\, j^{1/c}$, so $(\log j)^{c} \le c^{c} j$, and comparison with the
harmonic series applies.
\end{proof}

A bound of the shape $r_k(N) \le CN/(\log\log N)^{c}$ gives, at $N = 2^j$, terms
of order $1/(\log j)^{c}$. So no constant and no exponent rescues that shape: it
is insufficient \emph{as a shape}, not merely insufficiently strong.

\begin{proposition}[The stretched shape crosses at one]
\label{prop:stretch}
$\sum_j \exp\!\big(-(\log j)^{c}\big)$ diverges for $0 < c \le 1$ and converges
for $c > 1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
For $c \le 1$ the terms eventually exceed $1/j$, since
$(\log j)^{c} \le \log j$. For $c > 1$ we have $(\log j)^{c} \ge 2\log j$
eventually, so the terms are eventually at most $1/j^2$.
\end{proof}

A bound of the shape $r_k(N) \ll N\exp\!\big(-(\log\log N)^{c}\big)$ gives, at
$N = 2^j$, terms $\exp(-(\log j)^{c})$ up to the constant inside the logarithm.
By \Cref{prop:stretch} that shape closes the case precisely when $c > 1$, and
fails for every value at or below it.

\section{No power saving at $k = 3$}

\begin{theorem}[Roth]
\label{thm:roth}
$r_3(N) = o(N)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Behrend]
\label{thm:behrend}
\[
  r_3(N) \;\ge\; N \exp\!\big(-4\sqrt{\log N}\,\big).
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{corollary}
The decay in \Cref{thm:roth} is slower than any power of $N$: there is no
$\delta > 0$ with $r_3(N) = O(N^{1-\delta})$.
\end{corollary}

\begin{proof}
$\exp(-4\sqrt{\log N})$ exceeds $N^{-\delta} = \exp(-\delta \log N)$ for large
$N$, since $4\sqrt{\log N} < \delta \log N$ once $\log N > (4/\delta)^2$.
\end{proof}

Behrend's construction places points on a sphere in a high-dimensional grid,
where convexity forbids a midpoint; the dimension is tuned against the side
length, and that is where $\sqrt{\log N}$ enters. The corollary bounds what any
attempt on \Cref{thm:main} may hope for: the target is polylogarithmic, and
nothing polynomial is available to reach for.

\section{Position}

Against the published bounds, \Cref{thm:main} and the three threshold
propositions place each case exactly.

\begin{center}
\begin{tabularx}{\textwidth}{@{}lXl@{}}
\toprule
 & \textbf{best published bound} & \textbf{status under (R)} \\
\midrule
$k = 3$
  & $N/(\log N)^{1+c}$, absolute $c>0$ \cite{BloomSisask}
  & closed \\
$k = 4$
  & $N(\log N)^{-c}$, $0 < c \ll 1$ \cite{GreenTaoIII}
  & right shape, $c$ below $1$ \\
$k \ge 5$
  & $N\exp(-(\log\log N)^{c_k})$, $c_k \in (0,1)$ \cite{LSS}
  & right shape, $c_k$ below $1$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}

Bloom and Sisask state $|A| \ll N/(\log N)^{1+c}$ for an absolute $c > 0$:
exactly the shape \Cref{thm:main} consumes, past exponent one. Green and Tao
give $r_4(N) \ll N(\log N)^{-c}$ for an absolute $c > 0$, calling it the limit of
their methods, and their notational convention records $0 < c \ll 1$. Leng, Sah
and Sawhney fix $k \ge 5$ and give $c_k \in (0,1)$ with
$r_k(N) \ll N\exp(-(\log\log N)^{c_k})$; the interval is theirs.

So the two open cases are the same kind of thing. At $k = 4$ a polylogarithmic
exponent must cross one; at $k \ge 5$ a log-log exponent must. Neither is a
programme. Each is a single number in a published theorem, and in each the
authors state that their number is below the threshold.

Furstenberg's ergodic proof and Gowers's quantitative proof both establish the
(D) column of the older table, which \Cref{prop:strict} shows is a different
column. Green and Tao's theorem on progressions in the primes is a statement
about one specific set of density zero rather than about hypothesis (R) in
general. Gowers's general-$k$ bound has the shape $N/(\log\log N)^{c}$, which
\Cref{prop:loglog} rules out at every exponent.

\Cref{def:rk} through \Cref{thm:main}, and
\Cref{prop:edge}, \Cref{prop:loglog} and \Cref{prop:stretch}, are formalised in

import Mathlib

/-!
# The Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound on additive energy

`E(A) ≥ |A|⁴/|G|` for a finite abelian group `G` and `A ⊆ G`.

Elementary: the representation counts `r_A(x) = #{(a,b) ∈ A² : a + b = x}` sum to
`|A|²` across `|G|` points, so their squares cannot sum to less than the square
of the mean.

The statement is worth pinning because it is easy to misname. It is not the
Bloom–Sisask theorem, which bounds the size of a progression-free subset of
`[N]` by `C·N/(log N)^{1+c}`; no progression appears here at all. It is also
easy to state weaker than it is: `E(A) ≥ α³|G|`, with `α = |A|/|G|`, is implied
by this and falls short of it by a factor of `|A|·|G|`.

Everything is over `Finset` and ℕ-valued counts, deliberately. Phrasing it over
`Set G` with `Fintype ↑A` and a ℂ-valued indicator needs a `Decidable (x ∈ A)`
instance and a `Fintype` on the coercion that do not arrive on their own, and the
definitions fail to elaborate before any proof is reached.
-/

open Finset
open scoped BigOperators

noncomputable section
variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-- The additive-energy count: quadruples with `a + b = c + d`, counted as the
number of representations of each `x` as a sum of two elements of `A`, squared
and summed. Real-valued and stated over a `Finset`, so it elaborates without
choice-of-instance games on a `Set`. -/
def reps (A : Finset G) (x : G) : ℕ := (A ×ˢ A).filter (fun p => p.1 + p.2 = x) |>.card

def energy (A : Finset G) : ℕ := ∑ x : G, (reps A x) ^ 2

/-- Every pair contributes to exactly one `x`, so the representation counts sum
to `|A|²`. -/
theorem sum_reps (A : Finset G) : ∑ x : G, reps A x = A.card ^ 2 := by
  classical
  unfold reps
  rw [← Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise (f := fun p : G × G => p.1 + p.2)
      (s := A ×ˢ A) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset G)) (fun _ _ => Finset.mem_univ _)]
  · rw [Finset.card_product, sq]

/-- **The Cauchy–Schwarz lower bound on additive energy.**

`E(A) ≥ |A|⁴ / |G|`. The representation counts sum to `|A|²` over `|G|` points,
so squaring cannot be smaller than the square of the mean. This is the standard
bound, and it is the one an argument about energy actually uses; it is strictly
stronger than `E(A) ≥ α³|G|`, by a factor of `|A|·|G|`. -/
theorem energy_ge (A : Finset G) :
    (A.card : ℝ) ^ 4 / (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ≤ (energy A : ℝ) := by
  classical
  have hG : (0 : ℝ) < (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card G := Fintype.card_pos
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hcs : ((∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ))) ^ 2
      ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) * ∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    have := sq_sum_le_card_mul_sum_sq (s := (Finset.univ : Finset G))
      (f := fun x => (reps A x : ℝ))
    simpa using this
  have hsum : (∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ)) = (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    have h := sum_reps A
    calc (∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ)) = ((∑ x : G, reps A x : ℕ) : ℝ) := by push_cast; ring
      _ = ((A.card ^ 2 : ℕ) : ℝ) := by rw [h]
      _ = (A.card : ℝ) ^ 2 := by push_cast; ring
  rw [hsum] at hcs
  have hE : (energy A : ℝ) = ∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ) ^ 2 := by
    unfold energy; push_cast; ring
  rw [hE]
  rw [div_le_iff₀ hG]
  calc (A.card : ℝ) ^ 4 = ((A.card : ℝ) ^ 2) ^ 2 := by ring
    _ ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) * ∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ) ^ 2 := hcs
    _ = (∑ x : G, (reps A x : ℝ) ^ 2) * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by ring

#print axioms sum_reps
#print axioms energy_ge

end

A file arrived stating this bound over `Set G` with a ℂ-valued indicator and a
convolution. It did not compile — the definitions failed to elaborate for want of
`Decidable (x ∈ A)` and `Fintype ↑A`, `λ` was used as a binder (it is notation
for `fun`), and six `sorry`s carried the analytic content.

Repaired here rather than replaced: the same definitions, the same conclusion,
discharged. `convolution_eq_reps` is the bridge — the convolution of indicators
at `x` counts the representations of `x`, so the ℂ-valued energy is the ℕ-valued
one and `energy_ge` applies.
-/

namespace BloomSisaskSubmitted

open scoped Classical

noncomputable section
variable {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] [Fintype G] [DecidableEq G]

/-- Characteristic function of a set, taking values in ℂ. -/
def indicator (A : Set G) (x : G) : ℂ := if x ∈ A then 1 else 0

/-- Convolution of two functions on a finite group. -/
def convolution (f g : G → ℂ) (x : G) : ℂ := ∑ y : G, f y * g (x - y)

/-- The density of a set `A` in `G`. -/
def density (A : Set G) : ℝ := (A.toFinset.card : ℝ) / (Fintype.card G : ℝ)

/-- The additive energy of a set `A`. -/
def additive_energy (A : Set G) : ℝ :=
  ∑ x : G, ‖convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x‖ ^ 2

/-- The convolution of indicators counts representations. -/
theorem convolution_eq_reps (A : Set G) (x : G) :
    convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x = (reps A.toFinset x : ℂ) := by
  classical
  -- both sides count the same thing; name each count first
  set S : Finset G := Finset.univ.filter (fun y => y ∈ A ∧ x - y ∈ A) with hS
  have hL : convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x = (S.card : ℂ) := by
    unfold convolution indicator
    rw [hS, Finset.card_filter]
    push_cast
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro y _
    by_cases h1 : y ∈ A <;> by_cases h2 : x - y ∈ A <;> simp [h1, h2]
  have hcard : S.card = reps A.toFinset x := by
    unfold reps
    refine Finset.card_bij' (fun y _ => (y, x - y)) (fun p _ => p.1) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_
    · intro y hy
      rw [hS, Finset.mem_filter] at hy
      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Set.mem_toFinset]
      exact ⟨⟨hy.2.1, hy.2.2⟩, by abel⟩
    · intro p hp
      rw [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Set.mem_toFinset, Set.mem_toFinset] at hp
      rw [hS, Finset.mem_filter]
      refine ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, hp.1.1, ?_⟩
      have : x - p.1 = p.2 := by rw [← hp.2]; abel
      rw [this]; exact hp.1.2
    · intro y _; rfl
    · intro p hp
      rw [Finset.mem_filter] at hp
      have : x - p.1 = p.2 := by rw [← hp.2]; abel
      simp [this]
  rw [hL, hcard]

/-- The submitted conclusion, proved: `E(A) ≥ α³·|G|`.

Kept under the name it arrived with so the file it came from is fixed rather
than replaced, but the name is not accurate: this is the Cauchy–Schwarz lower
bound on additive energy, not the Bloom–Sisask theorem, which bounds a
progression-free subset of `[N]` by `C·N/(log N)^{1+c}` and involves no
convolution. It is also weaker than what the argument gives — `energy_ge`
supplies `|A|⁴/|G|`, and this follows from it by `|A|·|G| ≥ 1`. -/
theorem bloom_sisask_lemma (A : Set G) (h_nonempty : A.Nonempty) :
    additive_energy A ≥ density A ^ 3 * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
  classical
  set n : ℕ := A.toFinset.card with hn
  have hGpos : (0 : ℝ) < (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card G := Fintype.card_pos
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hn1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < n := by
      rw [hn, Finset.card_pos]
      exact (Set.toFinset_nonempty).mpr h_nonempty
    exact_mod_cast this
  have hG1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
    have : 0 < Fintype.card G := Fintype.card_pos
    exact_mod_cast this
  -- the ℂ energy is the ℕ energy
  have hEq : additive_energy A = (energy A.toFinset : ℝ) := by
    unfold additive_energy energy
    push_cast
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro x _
    rw [convolution_eq_reps]
    simp
  -- Cauchy–Schwarz, from the corpus
  have hCS : (n : ℝ) ^ 4 / (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ≤ (energy A.toFinset : ℝ) :=
    energy_ge A.toFinset
  -- and α³|G| ≤ |A|⁴/|G|, because |A|·|G| ≥ 1
  have hDens : density A ^ 3 * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 4 / (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by
    unfold density
    rw [div_pow, div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) hGpos]
    have h1 : (1 : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by nlinarith
    have hkey := mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_left h1
      (show (0:ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 3 * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ^ 2 by positivity)
    nlinarith [hkey]
  rw [hEq]
  exact le_trans hDens hCS


end
end BloomSisaskSubmitted

#print axioms BloomSisaskSubmitted.bloom_sisask_lemma

open scoped Classical

/-- Convolution of two functions on a finite group. -/

/-- The additive energy of a set `A`. -/

  ∑ x : G, ‖convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x‖ ^ 2

/-- The convolution of indicators counts representations. -/

    convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x = (reps A.toFinset x : ℂ) := by
  classical

  set S : Finset G := Finset.univ.filter (fun y => y ∈ A ∧ x - y ∈ A) with hS
  have hL : convolution (indicator A) (indicator A) x = (S.card : ℂ) := by
    unfold convolution indicator
    rw [hS, Finset.card_filter]
    push_cast
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro y _
    by_cases h1 : y ∈ A <;> by_cases h2 : x - y ∈ A <;> simp [h1, h2]

    unfold reps
    refine Finset.card_bij' (fun y _ => (y, x - y)) (fun p _ => p.1) ?_ ?_ ?_ ?_

    exact_mod_cast this

    unfold additive_energy energy
    push_cast
    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    intro x _
    rw [convolution_eq_reps]
    simp
  -- Cauchy–Schwarz, from the corpus
  have hCS : (n : ℝ) ^ 4 / (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ≤ (energy A.toFinset : ℝ) :=
    energy_ge A.toFinset
  -- and α³|G| ≤ |A|⁴/|G|, because |A|·|G| ≥ 1
  have hDens : density A ^ 3 * (Fintype.card G : ℝ) ≤ (n : ℝ) ^ 4 / (Fintype.card G : ℝ) := by

    rw [div_pow, div_mul_eq_mul_div, div_le_div_iff₀ (by positivity) hGpos]

\begin{document}
\title{\textbf{The Additive Energy of a Set Is at Least $|A|^4/|G|$}}
\author{C.\ Lando Mills\\
Trabuco Canyon, California\\
\texttt{c.landonmills@gmail.com}\\
ORCID: \href{https://orcid.org/0000-0003-0003-0552}{0000-0003-0003-0552}}
\date{17 August 2026}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
For a finite abelian group $G$ and $A \subseteq G$, the additive energy satisfies
$E(A) \ge |A|^4/|G|$. The proof is Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the representation
counts, which sum to $|A|^2$ across $|G|$ points: squares cannot sum to less than
the square of the mean.

Two things are worth pinning alongside it. The bound is often met in the weaker
form $E(A) \ge \alpha^3|G|$ with $\alpha = |A|/|G|$; that form follows from this
one and falls short of it by a factor of exactly $|A|\cdot|G|$. And the bound is
sometimes attached to the name Bloom--Sisask, which is a different theorem
about a different object --- it bounds a progression-free subset of $[N]$, and no
progression occurs anywhere below.
\end{abstract}

\section{The count}

Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and $A \subseteq G$.

\begin{definition}
\label{def:reps}
The \emph{representation count} of $x \in G$ is
\[
  r_A(x) \;=\; \#\{(a,b) \in A \times A \;:\; a + b = x\},
\]
and the \emph{additive energy} of $A$ is
\[
  E(A) \;=\; \sum_{x \in G} r_A(x)^2 .
\]
\end{definition}

$E(A)$ so defined counts the quadruples $(a,b,c,d) \in A^4$ with $a + b = c + d$,
sorted by the common value of the two sums. The two descriptions are the same
number, and the sorted one is what the argument uses.

\begin{lemma}[The counts sum to $|A|^2$]
\label{lem:sum}
$\displaystyle \sum_{x \in G} r_A(x) = |A|^2 .$
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The fibres of the map $A \times A \to G$, $(a,b) \mapsto a+b$, partition
$A \times A$, and $r_A(x)$ is the cardinality of the fibre over $x$. Summing
cardinalities over a partition returns $|A \times A| = |A|^2$.
\end{proof}

\Cref{lem:sum} is the whole of the input. It says the $|G|$ numbers $r_A(x)$
have mean $|A|^2/|G|$, and nothing else about $A$ is used again.

\section{The bound}

\begin{theorem}
\label{thm:energy}
For every $A \subseteq G$,
\[
  E(A) \;\ge\; \frac{|A|^4}{|G|}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
Cauchy--Schwarz over the index set $G$, applied to $r_A$ against the constant
function $1$, gives
\[
  \Big(\sum_{x \in G} r_A(x)\Big)^{\!2}
    \;\le\; |G| \sum_{x \in G} r_A(x)^2 .
\]
The left side is $|A|^4$ by \Cref{lem:sum} and the right side is $|G|\,E(A)$.
Divide by $|G| > 0$.
\end{proof}

Stated the other way: a family of nonnegative numbers with a fixed sum minimises
the sum of its squares when it is constant, and the constant value here is
$|A|^2/|G|$. The bound is what a set of that shape would have.

\begin{remark}[Equality]
\label{rem:equality}
Cauchy--Schwarz is an equality exactly when the two vectors are proportional, so
$E(A) = |A|^4/|G|$ holds precisely when $r_A$ is constant on $G$. The case
$A = G$ is one: $r_G(x) = |G|$ for every $x$, giving $E(G) = |G|^3 = |G|^4/|G|$.
So the bound is attained and cannot be improved as stated.
\end{remark}

\begin{remark}[When the bound says anything]
\label{rem:content}
Every set satisfies $E(A) \ge |A|^2$ for free, from the quadruples with $a = c$
and $b = d$. \Cref{thm:energy} improves on that free bound exactly when
$|A|^4/|G| > |A|^2$, that is when
\[
  |A| \;>\; \sqrt{|G|}, \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad \alpha > |G|^{-1/2}.
\]
Below the square-root threshold the diagonal count is the better of the two.
\end{remark}

\section{The weaker form, and the factor between them}

The bound is frequently stated in terms of the density $\alpha = |A|/|G|$ as
\[
  E(A) \;\ge\; \alpha^3 |G|.
\]

\begin{proposition}
\label{prop:weaker}
$\alpha^3|G| \le |A|^4/|G|$ for every nonempty $A$, and the ratio between the two
is exactly $|A|\cdot|G|$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Write $n = |A|$ and $N = |G|$. Then $\alpha^3 N = n^3/N^2$, while the bound of
\Cref{thm:energy} is $n^4/N$. Their quotient is
\[
  \frac{n^4/N}{n^3/N^2} \;=\; nN,
\]
which is at least $1$ whenever $A$ is nonempty.
\end{proof}

So the density form is a consequence of \Cref{thm:energy} and is weaker by a
factor that grows with both the set and the group. It is worth knowing which one
is in hand: an argument that needs $n^4/N$ is not served by $\alpha^3 N$, and the
gap between them is not a constant.

\section{The convolution phrasing}

Energy is often introduced through convolution rather than counting. With
$1_A : G \to \mathbb{C}$ the indicator and
\[
  (f * g)(x) \;=\; \sum_{y \in G} f(y)\, g(x-y),
\]
one sets $E(A) = \sum_{x \in G} \big| (1_A * 1_A)(x) \big|^2$.

\begin{lemma}
\label{lem:conv}
$(1_A * 1_A)(x) = r_A(x)$ for every $x \in G$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The summand $1_A(y)\,1_A(x-y)$ is $1$ when both $y \in A$ and $x - y \in A$, and
$0$ otherwise. So the sum counts the $y \in A$ with $x - y \in A$, and
$y \mapsto (y,\, x-y)$ is a bijection from those onto the pairs
$(a,b) \in A \times A$ with $a + b = x$, inverted by $(a,b) \mapsto a$.
\end{proof}

The two definitions of $E(A)$ therefore agree, and \Cref{thm:energy} applies to
either. \Cref{lem:conv} is the only place the group structure is used for
anything beyond addition being a map $G \times G \to G$.

\section{What this is not}

The bound above is sometimes filed under the name Bloom--Sisask. It is a
different statement about a different object. Bloom and Sisask bound the size of
a progression-free subset of $\{1, \dots, N\}$ by $CN/(\log N)^{1+c}$ for an
absolute $c > 0$; the theorem is about arithmetic progressions in the integers,
and its content is analytic. \Cref{thm:energy} is about quadruple counts in a
finite abelian group, mentions no progression, and its proof is Cauchy--Schwarz
in one line.

The confusion is intelligible --- energy bounds are among the tools used in that
literature --- and it is still a misattribution, which in a corpus that cites by
name is a defect rather than a loose end.

\section{Verification}

\Cref{def:reps}, \Cref{lem:sum}, \Cref{thm:energy} and \Cref{lem:conv} are
formalised in \Lean{} against Mathlib in
\texttt{Imscribing.Millennium.Erdos.AdditiveEnergy}, together with the density
form of \Cref{prop:weaker} derived from \Cref{thm:energy}. Counts are
$\mathbb{N}$-valued over \texttt{Finset}, and the conclusion is cast to
$\mathbb{R}$ only for the division. No result carries a \texttt{sorry}, and all
depend on \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice} and \texttt{Quot.sound}
alone.

\Cref{rem:equality} and \Cref{rem:content} are stated here and not formalised;
each is the arithmetic displayed in its proof.

\bibitem{TaoVu} T.~Tao and V.~Vu, \emph{Additive Combinatorics}, Cambridge
Studies in Advanced Mathematics \textbf{105}, Cambridge University Press, 2006,
\S2.3.

\bibitem{Gowers2001} W.~T.~Gowers, \emph{A new proof of Szemer\'edi's theorem},
Geom.\ Funct.\ Anal.\ \textbf{11} (2001), 465--588.

\bibitem{BloomSisask} T.~F.~Bloom and O.~Sisask, \emph{Breaking the logarithmic
barrier in Roth's theorem on arithmetic progressions}, preprint,
arXiv:2007.03528.
\end{thebibliography}

\end{document}
ENDBODY
